open_points.subject: record_change path policy for the SQLite database and its journal
open_points.text: - record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] Every file and directory under the data directory MUST be opened without following symbolic links, with os.O_NOFOLLOW and a directory also with os.O_DIRECTORY, whose presence is never tested (A20); a symbolic link met by any call after start makes that call raise StoreInternalError with nothing written.
open_points.other_text: - open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on data_directory itself, opened as a directory without following links and held for the life of the process, so the lock creates no file; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link; create its tables with create_store_schema, which leaves existing tables as they are; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue names — a trial case's file fixture is itself a StoredValue of file carriage (M21), so no other record names a value file —, which is a digest for which list_stored_value_rows_by_value_digest answers no row, and create the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.
open_points.question: Must the os.O_NOFOLLOW requirement exclude files opened internally by SQLite, including the database journal, or must the prompt provide a SQLite connection/VFS mechanism that opens those files with os.O_NOFOLLOW?
